messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PD-8921 fired: SEV3 - DedicatedPoolLatency for tenant=PulseHealth. Metric: p95 tail latency 1.8s (threshold 800ms). Reserved pool=ph-prod-1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-8921

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident created by alerting rule 'dedicated_pool_latency_v2'. Primary on-call: maya. Escalation policy: eng-oncall.sre.

maya (oncall): ack. I'm on it. pinging SRE and runtime. @jake @alex can you grab logs + routing?

jake (sre): on my way. pulling recent metrics from observability. Any customer impact notes from CSM? @lee

lee (csm): Just got a message from PulseHealth—users seeing slow responses to triage endpoint, some timeouts. They said it started ~5m ago after a small traffic surge. No data exfil.

alex (eng-runtime): looking at the pool ph-prod-1, I see autoscaler didn't spin up additional nodes — pool at 98% GPU mem due to many long context requests. KV cache evictions spiked. Suspect large-batch inference jobs holding workers.

maya (oncall): actions: 1) bump reserved capacity for ph-prod-1 by +2 gpus (if safe), 2) apply temporary rate-limit for heavy contexts, 3) failover high-latency requests to hosted fallback model. I'll attempt 1 now.

alex (eng-runtime): calling scale API:
```
POST /internal/scale/pools/ph-prod-1
{"delta_gpus": 2, "reason": "autoscale stuck - PD-8921"}
```
Response: 202 Accepted, scale started (op_id=op-5583).

jake (sre): digging into scheduler logs. There's a backlog in prewarm queue; several jobs stuck at 'allocating-kv-cache'. Logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:03:22Z scheduler[alloc] ERROR allocate: timeout waiting for kv-cache lock for model:llama-13b-quant
2026-03-15T12:03:24Z runtime[kv] WARN evicting 120MB from cache shard 3
```
Possible regression from recent kv-cache eviction change.

maya (oncall): good catch. @alex can we patch eviction policy to be less aggressive for dedicated pools? If not, can we roll back the last runtime config?

alex (eng-runtime): I can toggle a feature flag: `kv_eviction_aggressiveness=low` for ph-prod-1. Doing that now.

alex (eng-runtime): flag flipped. Noting: this is per-pool config, not global. Will monitor evictions.

pagerduty-bot: PD-8921 acknowledged by maya (oncall). Incident status: acknowledged. Waiting on updates.

ops-rotation: handoff note: I'm available for escalation if this hits PD-1. Current plan: monitor 10m after scale completes, then re-evaluate.

jake (sre): after scale op completed, we see CPU and GPU alloc back to normal, queue depth reduced. Metrics p95 down to 720ms. Errors dropped to baseline. KV eviction rate decreased.

maya (oncall): updating PulseHealth: "We've scaled your reserved pool and adjusted cache policy. Latencies are improving; we're continuing to watch for 10m."

lee (csm): PulseHealth confirmed improvement on their side. They saw successful requests and no more timeouts. Thanks for the quick response.

alex (eng-runtime): I'll keep the feature flag in place and open a PR to roll back the kv eviction change from last config deploy. Also scheduling a canary to validate eviction path for heavy-context workloads.

jake (sre): file follow-up ticket: RUNTIME-eviction-regen PD-8921. Assign to eng-runtime. Add regression tests for long-context jobs.

maya (oncall): final status: mitigated -> monitoring. Will close PD if stable for next 15m. Creating short blameless incident note.

pagerduty-bot: PD-8921 status changed to RESOLVED by maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): thanks team. Postmortem TODOs: - root cause: aggressive kv eviction + autoscaler hysteresis; - immediate mitigations: per-pool scale + flag flip; - long-term: autoscaler fix, regression tests, alert tuning to include kv-eviction spikes. I'll create the incident doc and link here.

lee (csm): I'll schedule a customer debrief with PulseHealth and share the postmortem once ready.

ops-rotation: handing back to normal rotation. Marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:

[system-note]: PD-8921 closed at 2026-03-15T12:15:70Z.
